source_title: Sahel Crisis 2012: Ensuring Food Security and Protecting Livelihoods, Information Note No. 1
issuer: FAO Sub-regional Emergency and Rehabilitation Office, West Africa/Sahel
place: Sahel region (CILSS aggregate); Chad, Mauritania, Senegal
reading: Sahel cereal 16.6 million tonnes in 2011/12, 25 percent below the 2010/11 record and 2 percent below the previous five years. Chad, Mauritania and Senegal fell 50, 52 and 31 percent from 2010/11. A footnote revises Chad to -39 percent nationally. The aggregate is the CILSS Sahel, not the ten workbook countries, and it is a forecast.

source_title: Haiti's damaged food sector slowly begins to mend
issuer: FAO Newsroom, reporting the FAO/WFP Crop and Food Security Assessment Mission
causes_named_by_source: January 2010 earthquake; late start of the spring rains
reading: FAO/WFP forecast 2010 cereals at 503,600 tonnes, 9 percent below 2009. Spring maize fell 8 percent and sorghum 4 percent from 2009. Irrigated rice was expected up 15 percent. Earthquake damage and a late rainy season are named together. The mission report itself was not opened.

causes_named_by_source: poor rains associated with the El Niño episode
reading: FAO puts 2015 rice at 3.2 million tonnes, 4 percent below the 2014 record, and maize at 1.1 million tonnes, 5 percent below 2014, after poor El Niño rains. The 20 December 2016 brief gives 2016 paddy at 4 million tonnes, a 5 percent recovery; rice and paddy are not the same unit.

source_title: Special Report: FAO/GIEWS Crop Assessment Mission to Liberia
reading: 1995 rice was at most 23 percent of the pre-civil-war level (Table 1: 56,196 to 64,426 tonnes). The mission calls its estimates highly tentative, with no systematic survey since 1989.

source_title: FAO/WFP Crop and Food Supply Assessment Mission to Liberia
causes_named_by_source: war and displacement; small plots; rebel incursions in Lofa
reading: 2000 paddy 144,000 tonnes against 259,000 in 1988; milled 94,000 tonnes is 55 percent of pre-war. No official crop data has been collected since 1989, and the mission assumed 500 kg per household.
